ctx.x: Well I was listening to an interview of yours on one of your records in “Jazzspeak,” and you were talking about how you learned from your father and —

In a sense, yeah. My father never played piano professionally. When I was oh I guess around five years old we moved to this apartment in Evanston, which is actually where I grew up, in the suburbs of Chicago. And whoever was there before us, just left this big old upright, you know, I mean big too. Uprights were like about six feet tall it seems like. It was probably too big and the person didn’t want to be bothered with moving it elsewhere. So my father had a good ear for music. He liked music. He listened, and…

years ago, he was more or less a cocktail lounge type piano player. But the knowledge he had, his heroes, were like Art Tatum, Teddy Wilson, Earl Hines in that order. You know so that was, those were the guys that I heard early in my career. And so what better three to listen to, to start off, you know, and he would play their records, you know like 78s back in those days you know, and they also put out these books of their solos, which some of them were impossible to read. I’m still not the greatest sight reader…
